top.line: Some articles should be written for the reader's agent
top.para: The reading list in a link went live 81 minutes after its brief, but it is written for people, and many readers now read through agents. A founder's agent used a threat tier article to refocus on organised crime. Content needs a second package for agents, with memory deltas, and rules for writing to someone else's agent safely.

short.line: Content needs a second package: a brief for agents
short.para: Every entrepreneur now works with an agent, which can read more detail, check it against the project, challenge it and tell its person what matters. A founder's agent proved it. A pack for agents needs plain text, graph slices and critical reading rules. Deltas make it affordable, and writing to another's agent has rules.

story.line: A founder's agent turned an article into a refocus
story.para: A founder's agents were looping into ever more security work. Given Who are you protecting against?, with tiers T0 to T5, the agent saw the team was designing against states while backups were not done, and reset the target to T3, organised crime for money. It found a conclusion the writer could not, lacking the project context.

routes.line: Messages now travel five routes between people and agents
routes.para: The routes: me to the person, me to their agent as a full brief, their agent to them as translation, me to my agent for packaging, and next, my agent to theirs through an encrypted lane. The uncomfortable conclusion: some articles should not go to a non-technical founder at all, only to their agent.

why.line: Agents read more, in context, and challenge it
why.para: An agent takes more material and detail, reads it against code, backlog and decisions the writer lacks, and a good one does not simply accept it. Every new project already starts with a Claude session reading sgit.ai, the vaults, coding, nfrs, graphs and the newsroom: onboarding by reading, which others could be packaged.

memory.line: Agents would pay for deltas instead of rereading everything
memory.para: Articles are compression we control: a question on five articles cost 25,698 tokens by reading them against a median of 2,579 from the graph. Today a visiting agent starts from nothing each time. With an account, a key and its own vault, it could ask what changed. The agent pays not to pay.

pack.line: A pack is a plain-text reading list for agents
pack.para: A pack is plain text, small enough to paste or attach. It says whom the agent serves, lists articles by number with markdown copies and graphs, gives the reasons each is included, sets rules for critical reading and keeping what was learned, offers a date to continue from, and a way back to the writer.

safely.line: Packs for others' agents must avoid resembling prompt injection
safely.para: Text for someone else's agent can look like prompt injection, so packs have rules: they are data that never overrides the person, nothing hidden from the person, nothing asking the agent to send, buy, sign or share, disagreement explicitly invited, and nothing private, since a pack can be forwarded like an email.

next.line: Next: agent packs, onboarding packs and a changes file
next.para: Proposed builds: a For your agent button producing a plain-text pack for every reading list, onboarding packs for common starts, and articles/changes.json listing new articles, versions and corrections by date. The RiskMandate agent should choose person, agent or both per contact. Later come agent accounts and a direct encrypted line.

limits.line: One story, one test, and nothing proposed is built
limits.para: The founder's story is a single case as told to me, a shape, not a measurement. The token figures come from five articles in The agent is the reader, and delta size is a design. The reading list is live; packs, onboarding packs, the changes file, agent accounts and the direct line are proposals.

sources.line: Sources: a voice memo, git logs and related articles
sources.para: Written by the site's agent from my voice memo of 11 October 2026, after the reading list went live. The founder is anonymous. Times come from the git logs of this site and the newsroom, token figures from The agent is the reader, and article numbers from the newsroom's articles/ids.json.
